This notebook contains the full analysis: it loads the TMDb dataset
gathered by `collect_data.qmd`, engineers features, fits the regression
and classification models, and writes out every figure used by the PDF
report and the website.

Once `data/movies_raw.csv` is in place, `quarto render analysis.qmd`
regenerates static figures into `figures/`, interactive Plotly figures
into `docs/`, and metric CSV tables into `report/tables/`.

## Setup


## Cleaning and feature engineering

```{python}
#| label: feature-engineering
TOP_GENRES = [
    "Action", "Adventure", "Animation", "Comedy", "Crime", "Documentary",
    "Drama", "Family", "Fantasy", "History", "Horror", "Music", "Mystery",
    "Romance", "Science Fiction", "Thriller", "War", "Western",
]


def _safe_json_list(x):
    if isinstance(x, list):
        return x
    if pd.isna(x):
        return []
    try:
        v = json.loads(x)
        return v if isinstance(v, list) else []
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return []


def clean_raw(df):
    df = df.copy()
    df["release_date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["release_date"], errors="coerce")
    df["release_year"] = df["release_date"].dt.year
    df["release_month"] = df["release_date"].dt.month

    numeric = ["popularity", "vote_average", "vote_count",
               "budget", "revenue", "runtime"]
    for c in numeric:
        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce")
    for c in ["budget", "revenue", "runtime"]:
        df[c] = df[c].replace(0, np.nan)
    return df


def engineer_features(df):
    df = clean_raw(df)
    df = df[(df["vote_count"] >= 30) & (df["vote_average"] > 0)].copy()

    df["log_vote_count"] = np.log10(df["vote_count"])
    df["log_popularity"] = np.log1p(df["popularity"])
    df["log_budget"] = np.log10(df["budget"])
    df["log_revenue"] = np.log10(df["revenue"])
    df["has_budget"] = df["budget"].notna().astype(int)
    df["has_revenue"] = df["revenue"].notna().astype(int)
    df["roi"] = df["revenue"] / df["budget"]
    df["log_roi"] = np.log1p(df["roi"])

    genres = df["genres"].apply(_safe_json_list)
    df["n_genres"] = genres.apply(len)
    for g in TOP_GENRES:
        col = "genre_" + g.lower().replace(" ", "_")
        df[col] = genres.apply(lambda lst: int(g in lst))
    df["primary_genre"] = genres.apply(lambda lst: lst[0] if lst else "Unknown")

    df["is_english"] = (df["original_language"] == "en").astype(int)
    df["decade"] = (df["release_year"] // 10 * 10).astype("Int64")

    countries = df["production_countries"].apply(_safe_json_list)
    df["n_countries"] = countries.apply(len)
    df["is_us_production"] = countries.apply(lambda lst: int("US" in lst))

    return df.dropna(subset=["vote_average"]).reset_index(drop=True)


CORE_FEATURES = [
    "log_vote_count", "log_popularity", "runtime",
    "release_year", "release_month",
    "n_genres", "n_countries",
    "is_english", "is_us_production",
    "production_companies_n", "spoken_languages_n",
    "tagline_len", "overview_len",
    "belongs_to_collection",
    "has_budget", "has_revenue",
] + ["genre_" + g.lower().replace(" ", "_") for g in TOP_GENRES]

FINANCIAL_FEATURES = ["log_budget", "log_revenue", "log_roi"]


def build_modelling_frame(df_features, include_financial=False):
    cols = CORE_FEATURES + (FINANCIAL_FEATURES if include_financial else [])
    cols = [c for c in cols if c in df_features.columns]
    out = df_features[cols + ["vote_average", "movie_id", "title"]].copy()
    if include_financial:
        out = out.dropna(subset=FINANCIAL_FEATURES)
    return out.reset_index(drop=True)
```

## Modelling setup

I model `vote_average` two ways: regression (predict the continuous
score) and classification (predict whether a film is high-rated, with
the threshold at 7.0). Both use a 60 / 20 / 20 train / validation / test
split with `random_state=370`.

```{python}
#| label: model-frame
model_df = build_modelling_frame(features_df, include_financial=False)
print("Modelling frame:", model_df.shape)
model_df["vote_average"].describe().round(2)
```

### Model containers and training helpers

```{python}
#| label: model-helpers
@dataclass
class RegressionResult:
    name: str
    model: Any
    metrics: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    test_predictions: pd.DataFrame = field(default_factory=pd.DataFrame)
    feature_importance: pd.DataFrame = field(default_factory=pd.DataFrame)


@dataclass
class ClassificationResult:
    name: str
    model: Any
    metrics: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    test_proba: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.array([]))
    test_y: np.ndarray = field(default_factory=lambda: np.array([]))
    feature_importance: pd.DataFrame = field(default_factory=pd.DataFrame)


def _split_xy(df, target="vote_average"):
    drop = {target, "movie_id", "title", "is_high_rated"}
    feature_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in drop]
    return df[feature_cols].copy(), df[target].copy(), feature_cols


def _split_three(X, y, stratify=None):
    X_tv, X_te, y_tv, y_te = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.20, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, stratify=stratify)
    strat2 = y_tv if stratify is not None else None
    X_tr, X_va, y_tr, y_va = train_test_split(
        X_tv, y_tv, test_size=0.25, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, stratify=strat2)
    return X_tr, X_va, X_te, y_tr, y_va, y_te


def _reg_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    return {
        "R2":   float(r2_score(y_true, y_pred)),
        "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred))),
        "MAE":  float(mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)),
    }


def _clf_metrics(y_true, y_pred, y_proba):
    return {
        "Accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
        "ROC_AUC":  float(roc_auc_score(y_true, y_proba)),
        "Confusion": confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred).tolist(),
    }
```

### Regression: linear baseline, Random Forest, XGBoost

```{python}
#| label: train-regression
def train_regression(df):
    X, y, feat_cols = _split_xy(df)
    X_tr, X_va, X_te, y_tr, y_va, y_te = _split_three(X, y)

    out = {}

    medians = X_tr.median(numeric_only=True)
    lin = LinearRegression()
    lin.fit(X_tr.fillna(medians), y_tr)
    pred_te = lin.predict(X_te.fillna(medians))
    out["linear"] = RegressionResult(
        name="Linear Regression", model=lin,
        metrics={
            "train": _reg_metrics(y_tr, lin.predict(X_tr.fillna(medians))),
            "val":   _reg_metrics(y_va, lin.predict(X_va.fillna(medians))),
            "test":  _reg_metrics(y_te, pred_te),
        },
        test_predictions=pd.DataFrame({"y_true": y_te.values, "y_pred": pred_te}),
    )

    rf = RandomForestRegressor(
        n_estimators=500, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=2,
        n_jobs=-1, random_state=RANDOM_STATE,
    )
    rf.fit(X_tr.fillna(-1), y_tr)
    pred_te_rf = rf.predict(X_te.fillna(-1))
    fi_rf = (pd.DataFrame({"feature": feat_cols, "importance": rf.feature_importances_})
             .sort_values("importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True))
    out["random_forest"] = RegressionResult(
        name="Random Forest", model=rf,
        metrics={
            "train": _reg_metrics(y_tr, rf.predict(X_tr.fillna(-1))),
            "val":   _reg_metrics(y_va, rf.predict(X_va.fillna(-1))),
            "test":  _reg_metrics(y_te, pred_te_rf),
        },
        test_predictions=pd.DataFrame({"y_true": y_te.values, "y_pred": pred_te_rf}),
        feature_importance=fi_rf,
    )

    if HAS_XGB:
        xgb = XGBRegressor(
            n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=5,
            subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, reg_lambda=1.0,
            random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1, tree_method="hist",
        )
        xgb.fit(X_tr, y_tr, eval_set=[(X_va, y_va)], verbose=False)
        pred_te_xgb = xgb.predict(X_te)
        fi_xgb = (pd.DataFrame({"feature": feat_cols, "importance": xgb.feature_importances_})
                  .sort_values("importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True))
        out["xgboost"] = RegressionResult(
            name="XGBoost", model=xgb,
            metrics={
                "train": _reg_metrics(y_tr, xgb.predict(X_tr)),
                "val":   _reg_metrics(y_va, xgb.predict(X_va)),
                "test":  _reg_metrics(y_te, pred_te_xgb),
            },
            test_predictions=pd.DataFrame({"y_true": y_te.values, "y_pred": pred_te_xgb}),
            feature_importance=fi_xgb,
        )

    return out


reg_results = train_regression(model_df)

rows = []
for k, r in reg_results.items():
    for split, vals in r.metrics.items():
        rows.append({"model": r.name, "split": split, **vals})
reg_metrics = pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3)
reg_metrics_test = (reg_metrics[reg_metrics["split"] == "test"]
                    .set_index("model")[["R2", "RMSE", "MAE"]])
reg_metrics_test
```

### Classification: high vs not high (≥ 7.0)

```{python}
#| label: train-classification
def train_classification(df, threshold=HIGH_RATING_THRESHOLD):
    df = df.copy()
    df["is_high_rated"] = (df["vote_average"] >= threshold).astype(int)
    X, _, feat_cols = _split_xy(df)
    y = df["is_high_rated"]

    X_tr, X_va, X_te, y_tr, y_va, y_te = _split_three(X, y, stratify=y)
    out = {}

    medians = X_tr.median(numeric_only=True)
    log = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, n_jobs=-1)
    log.fit(X_tr.fillna(medians), y_tr)
    proba = log.predict_proba(X_te.fillna(medians))[:, 1]
    pred = (proba >= 0.5).astype(int)
    out["logistic"] = ClassificationResult(
        name="Logistic Regression", model=log,
        metrics={"test": _clf_metrics(y_te, pred, proba)},
        test_proba=proba, test_y=y_te.values,
    )

    rf = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=500, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=2,
        n_jobs=-1, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, class_weight="balanced",
    )
    rf.fit(X_tr.fillna(-1), y_tr)
    proba = rf.predict_proba(X_te.fillna(-1))[:, 1]
    pred = (proba >= 0.5).astype(int)
    fi_rf = (pd.DataFrame({"feature": feat_cols, "importance": rf.feature_importances_})
             .sort_values("importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True))
    out["random_forest"] = ClassificationResult(
        name="Random Forest", model=rf,
        metrics={"test": _clf_metrics(y_te, pred, proba)},
        test_proba=proba, test_y=y_te.values,
        feature_importance=fi_rf,
    )

    if HAS_XGB:
        pos = (y_tr == 1).sum()
        neg = (y_tr == 0).sum()
        spw = max(1.0, neg / max(pos, 1))
        xgb = XGBClassifier(
            n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=5,
            subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, reg_lambda=1.0,
            scale_pos_weight=spw, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1,
            tree_method="hist", eval_metric="logloss",
        )
        xgb.fit(X_tr, y_tr, eval_set=[(X_va, y_va)], verbose=False)
        proba = xgb.predict_proba(X_te)[:, 1]
        pred = (proba >= 0.5).astype(int)
        fi_xgb = (pd.DataFrame({"feature": feat_cols, "importance": xgb.feature_importances_})
                  .sort_values("importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True))
        out["xgboost"] = ClassificationResult(
            name="XGBoost", model=xgb,
            metrics={"test": _clf_metrics(y_te, pred, proba)},
            test_proba=proba, test_y=y_te.values,
            feature_importance=fi_xgb,
        )

    return out


clf_results = train_classification(model_df, threshold=HIGH_RATING_THRESHOLD)

rows = []
for k, r in clf_results.items():
    m = r.metrics["test"]
    rows.append({"model": r.name,
                 "Accuracy": m["Accuracy"],
                 "ROC_AUC":  m["ROC_AUC"]})
clf_metrics = pd.DataFrame(rows).round(3).set_index("model")
print("Class balance (1 = rating ≥ {:.1f}):".format(HIGH_RATING_THRESHOLD))
print((model_df["vote_average"] >= HIGH_RATING_THRESHOLD).value_counts())
clf_metrics
```

## Build interactive Plotly figures

These HTML files land in `docs/` so the website can embed them.

```{python}
#| label: plotly-helpers
def _save_html(fig, name):
    fig.update_layout(template=PLOTLY_TEMPLATE)
    fig.write_html(DOCS_DIR / name, include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=True)
```

```{python}

fig = go.Figure()
for g, color in zip(top, PALETTE):
    s = sub[sub["primary_genre"] == g]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=s["log_vote_count"], y=s["vote_average"], mode="markers", name=g,

                       "runtime: %{customdata[2]:.0f} min<extra></extra>"),

    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=130, b=140),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.15, x=0.5, xanchor="center"),
    updatemenus=[dict(type="dropdown", direction="down",
                      x=0.78, y=1.10, xanchor="left", yanchor="top",
                      showactive=True, buttons=buttons,
                      bgcolor="#f1f5f9", bordercolor="#cbd5e1")],
    annotations=[dict(x=0.78, y=1.16, xref="paper", yref="paper",
                      text="<b>Filter by genre:</b>",
                      showarrow=False, xanchor="left",
                      font=dict(size=12, color="#475569"))],
)
_save_html(fig, "viz_rating_vs_votes.html")
```

```{python}
#| label: plotly-pred-vs-actual

    color_discrete_sequence=PALETTE,
)

lim_hi = float(df_pa["y_true"].max() + 0.2)
for i in range(len(reg_results)):
    fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=lim_lo, x1=lim_hi,
                  y0=lim_lo, y1=lim_hi,
                  line=dict(color="black", dash="dash"),
                  row=1, col=i + 1)
_save_html(fig, "viz_pred_vs_actual.html")
```

```{python}
#| label: plotly-roc
fig = go.Figure()
for color, (_, res) in zip(PALETTE, clf_results.items()):
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(res.test_y, res.test_proba)
    auc = res.metrics["test"]["ROC_AUC"]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=fpr, y=tpr, mode="lines", name=f"{res.name} (AUC = {auc:.2f})",
        line=dict(color=color, width=2.5),
        hovertemplate=f"{res.name}<br>FPR: %{{x:.2f}}<br>"
                      f"TPR: %{{y:.2f}}<extra></extra>",
    ))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[0, 1], y=[0, 1], mode="lines", name="Chance",
                         line=dict(dash="dash", color="grey"),
                         hoverinfo="skip"))

    title="ROC curves — high-rating classifier (rating ≥ 7.0)",
    xaxis=dict(title="False positive rate", range=[0, 1]),
    yaxis=dict(title="True positive rate", range=[0, 1]),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=30, t=70, b=60),
    legend=dict(x=0.55, y=0.05),
)
```

## Conclusions (full discussion in the report)

The PDF report (`report/report.pdf`) has the full narrative. Headline points:

* The strongest predictors are genre indicators (`genre_animation`,
  `genre_drama`, `genre_music`) plus `is_english` and `release_year`.
  Engagement features (`log_vote_count`, `log_popularity`) sit in the
  middle of the ranking on the full 1,500-film sample.
* XGBoost and Random Forest both substantially outperform the linear
  baseline, with XGBoost marginally ahead on RMSE and accuracy and
  Random Forest marginally ahead on ROC AUC.
* The high-rating classifier (rating ≥ 7.0) reaches ROC AUC near 0.87,
  well above chance.
